answer: Residual memory pricing: each identity carries a decaying balance of shared pool draws. Registering downstream identities consumes pool credit faster than linear, so the marginal clone pays a rising fraction of the juniper pool's remaining capacity. Colluders face superlinear credit exhaustion, forcing fresh capital or dormant onyx reserves to reset. Enforcement is automatic at the meadow ledger layer, where depleted credit halts new registrations.
